walkthrough:
Rewrite the equation $|z + 3 - 2\mathrm{i}| = 2$ in the standard circle form $|z - z_0| = r$:
$$|z - (-3 + 2\mathrm{i})| = 2$$

Identify the geometrical properties of the locus:
The locus represents a circle with centre at $(-3, 2)$ (representing the complex number $-3 + 2\mathrm{i}$) and radius $r = 2$.

Determine the key points and axes intercepts:
The centre lies in the second quadrant at $x = -3, y = 2$.
Because the radius is $2$, the lowest point of the circle is at $(-3, 2 - 2) = (-3, 0)$, touching the real axis tangentially.
The circle spans horizontally from $x = -5$ to $x = -1$, and vertically from $y = 0$ to $y = 4$.
Draw an unshaded circle with centre $(-3, 2)$ and radius $2$ on the Argand diagram with labelled real and imaginary axes.

hints: The least $|z|$ is the shortest distance from the origin to the circle found in part (a).
Find the distance from the origin to the centre $(-3,2)$ using Pythagoras.
Because the origin lies outside the radius-$2$ circle, subtract the radius from the centre-to-origin distance and keep the result exact.
walkthrough: Interpret $|z|$ geometrically as the distance from the origin $(0, 0)$ to any point $z$ on the circle.

Calculate the distance $d$ from the origin to the centre of the circle $(-3, 2)$:
$$d = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{9 + 4} = \sqrt{13}$$

Compare $d$ with the radius $r = 2$:
Since $d = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.606 > 2$, the origin lies strictly outside the circle.

Calculate the least distance from the origin to the circle by subtracting the radius from $d$:
$$\text{Least } |z| = d - r = \sqrt{13} - 2$$
